layers.converts: Fuel, wind, sun and atoms into electricity delivered to the data-centre fence.
layers.paid: Regulated returns on a growing rate base, long-term power contracts, and multi-year equipment backlogs.
layers.scarce: Grid hookups, gas turbines, transformers, permits and skilled trades.
layers.multiple: Contracted load growth. Utilities that used to trade like bonds now trade on growth.

layers.converts: Electricity into computation (FLOPs) and the memory that feeds it.
layers.paid: Price times volume. Whoever controls the scarcest part sets the price.
layers.scarce: Leading-edge wafers, advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory, lithography tools, and now optics.
layers.multiple: Forward earnings and the debate over where the cycle peaks. Memory is cheap at the peak, by design.

layers.converts: Thousands of chips into one working machine: buildings, power gear, cooling, networks, storage.
layers.paid: Construction and equipment backlogs, hardware shipments, rental and capacity contracts.
layers.scarce: Powered land, cooling, fibre and optical links, storage, and the crews to build it.
layers.multiple: Visibility of backlog, which tracks hyperscaler capex guidance quarter by quarter.

layers.converts: Computing capacity into intelligence, sold as tokens through clouds, APIs and subscriptions.
layers.paid: Cloud rental, usage-based API fees, subscriptions and advertising lift.
layers.scarce: Compute, research talent, data, and the cash to keep spending.
layers.multiple: Cloud growth against capex intensity. The market pays for revenue that outruns the spend.

layers.converts: Tokens into value: new revenue, lower costs, better products for the end customer.
layers.paid: Subscriptions, transactions, ads, devices and productivity gains.
layers.scarce: The customer relationship, proprietary data, and a place in the daily workflow.
layers.multiple: Proof that AI adds revenue rather than cannibalising it. Seat-based software is on trial.

principles.t: Demand outruns supply at every link
principles.b: Each conversion needs the output of the one below it, and every link is short at the same time. The **scarcest link earns scarcity pricing**, which is why valuations can run hot without the cycle being over.

principles.t: The bottleneck moves, so money moves
principles.b: Fix one constraint and the next one binds. GPUs gave way to packaging, then power, then memory and optics. **Rotation is the normal state of this market**, across players inside a layer and across layers.

principles.t: Value climbs the stack over time
principles.b: The base layers get paid first. As the cost per token falls, the layers that **own the customer** capture more of the margin. Owning the whole conversion means not having to guess which link wins next.

migration.sub: Each year the binding constraint sat in a different place, and leadership rotated with it. The dashed card is the next candidate, not a forecast.

steps.w: CoWoS capacity and high-bandwidth memory capped shipments.
Turbines, transformers and interconnection queues became the limit.
DRAM and NAND shortages, fibre and optical links, local permit fights.
The stack needs end revenue that justifies the capex.
